Maya: Heads up — seeing intermittent 502/504s hitting /infer on us-west-edge that back to the headless service `inference-svc.edge`. Seems to spike right after GPU pool scales up :thinking:
Ahmad: Do you have cluster dumps or `kubectl get endpointslice` when it happens? kube-proxy mode on edge nodes (ipvs/iptables)?
Maya: Quick dump from right after a scale: 
```
$ kubectl get endpointslice -n edge -l kubernetes.io/service-name=inference-svc -o wide
NAME                          ADDRESSTYPE   PORTS   ENDPOINTS
inference-svc-abcde           IPv4          8080    10.0.5.12,10.0.5.13
inference-svc-fghij           IPv4          8080    10.0.6.3
```
But new GPU nodes (10.0.6.x) were running pods but not appearing consistently in slices for ~45-90s. `kubectl describe pods` shows readiness probe failing for the sidecar for ~30s while CUDA driver init completes.
Zack: Could be two-ish things: (1) readiness probe timing -> endpoint not created, (2) NLB target registration delay so node traffic heads to targets that aren't ready. Edge runs kube-proxy in ipvs mode and we see conntrack entries sticking around. Have you checked `conntrack -L` on nodes?
SRE Oncall: infra-bot logged autoscaler events: autoscaler launched 3 gpus at 12:34 UTC, AWS NLB showed `Target 10.0.6.3:8080 registering` for ~120s before healthy. EndpointSlice controller also throttled around then (controller backoff).
Ahmad: Quick workaround that helped: restart kube-proxy on the new node after pods are ready, traffic comes back immediately. Command: `kubectl -n kube-system delete pod -l k8s-app=kube-proxy --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>` (we did this on one node and recovery was instant) :hammer:
Maya: Confirmed — restarting kube-proxy on one problem node recovered traffic. But that's a manual step and not acceptable at scale.
Zack: Long term fixes to consider: make the inference sidecar readiness wait on driver init (so endpoints only published when truly ready), set NLB target deregistration/registration timeouts tighter, and increase EndpointSlice/controller QPS to reduce reconciliation lag after scale events. Also check `--node-status-update-frequency` and controller-manager QPS.
Maya: I think main root cause is ordering: node + pod become schedulable, CNI attaches IP, pod is Running but sidecar readiness false while driver comes up; NLB starts health checks that fail and node sits in PENDING, EndpointSlice controller sees pod not Ready so not included -> short window where clients hit service records that map to real IPs but NLB routes to unhealthy targets -> 502s.
SRE Oncall: Agreed. Actionable plan: 1) add explicit readiness gating in the inference helm chart so readiness fails until GPU drivers + sidecar fully up; 2) adjust autoscaler lifecycle hook to wait for Kubelet readiness before announcing nodes to LB (or use target registration health checks); 3) bump endpoint-slice-controller client QPS/resync for edge clusters; 4) run a scale test with synthetic load to validate.
Ahmad: I'll open a PR to add a `pre-warm` init container that blocks readiness and also add a post-scale job that runs `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/kube-proxy -n kube-system` across newly launched nodes if registration latency > 60s.
Zack: Also add metric/alert: `endpointslice.controller.reconcile.latency` and NLB target registration time, so we detect this window automatically.
infra-bot: [autoscaler] launched 3 nodes pool=gpu-edge-uswest at 2026-03-17T12:34:11Z; NLB target registration delayed 95s average in last 10m.
Maya: Created a short runbook entry under eng-infra -> edge -> headless-scaling with quick triage steps (check endpointslice, restart kube-proxy on node if needed, validate readiness probes).
SRE Oncall: Great. We'll schedule a canary scale tomorrow and follow the plan. :thumbsup:
